review.scope: Static schema/reference/document ownership, scoped UI IDs and minimal/null activation, render state/lifecycle and cloud motion. Final native UI capture waits for actual form drawing.

limitations: Saved test-only content is retained separately after replacement confirmation and never merged automatically. Native marker checks demonstrate detection, while the progress case checks storage identity and an absent/unchanged source file rather than every existing save format.

Inspector navigation supports registered common-event and level-property definitions plus generic workspace activation. Teleporter/actor definition adapters remain pending; local instance editing stays available.

Wind fields currently emit horizontal acceleration requests and loop lifecycle notifications. Actor motion coupling, spatial field placement, sound/particle assignment and regional weather bindings are separate prerequisites; definitions do not apply a global force.

Common events support17 registered native operations with explicit action calls only. Automatic/parallel scheduling, execution-switch triggers, nested calls, loops/scripts, advanced variable operands and message commands need separate runtime bindings. Actor-template registry is currently empty.

Existing state scopes and narrower variable ranges require explicit save migrations; this slice permits stable-scope defaults/names and widening ranges only. Explicit saved values override defaults; absent keys use the current definition.
Dialogue uses the existing 2–64-choice runtime contract. Standalone messages, cancellation handlers/redirects and per-message style/position/concurrency options need later runtime bindings.
New level creation includes its terrain and starter sequence. Other record creation, deletion, storage/slot migrations and additional effect types remain pending.
Saved definitions take effect in a fresh test/session. Save All commits records individually and reports partial success; interdependent edits require dependency order.
HP is live. MP remains an explicit preview fixture until its resource service is bound.
Native input checks use owned adapter events. Physical gamepad/hotplug feel remains hands-on review.
Generated v1/v2 legacy fixtures and current v3 checks do not certify every historical user save. Older previews cannot read v3 ability-removal saves.
Broader authoring surfaces, full original editor parity, multiplayer viewports and soundboard authoring remain separate milestones.
Indexed level/sequence JSON is authoritative; legacy compiled levels and .qst parsing remain fallbacks for unregistered projects/routes.

Creation uses shared starter assets and the default player fixture; it checks those dependencies but does not yet prove complete dependency closure. Both index versions must fit1MiB. Conflicting/unknown recovery is preserved and requires resolution.
New projects copy the curated bundled starter content. Empty-game presets and a general asset-management UI remain later surfaces.

Open project requires the native powersurge.project.json format. Arbitrary legacy projects and retained raw laboratory folders are not adopted in place; the protected historical user project was not migrated.

Save Project writes records and level edits individually, then entry settings; partial failures preserve earlier successful commits. Save project copy creates a fresh identity, copies content/current entry and excludes local progress/recovery.

Project snapshot copying retains the current20,000-file/2GiB total and512MiB individual-asset bounds. Generated storage uses8MiB per-output bounds; larger generator output needs a binary-write extension.
Project-history metadata is one portable .userdata file. Local state, reports and retained user projects are excluded from release input.
Physical mouse/keyboard usability remains reviewable in the included project dialogs; native automation verifies service transitions and rendered availability, not every OS interaction.

Existing projects without indexed rendering records retain legacy behavior. This update does not silently install/migrate their data. Bundled projects include indexed rendering records; builds predating these record kinds require explicit migration.

Material libraries are one shared document with protected attachment/member identity/order. Material creation/removal, general per-shape lighting overrides, direct member-ID inspector handoff and a general rendering-record installer remain subsequent surfaces.

Trusted-source shader profiles remain metadata-only. This adapter only executes its registered builtin kernel. GPU verification covers the current Windows OpenGL build, not browser/GLES/platform certification or a sustained performance milestone.
Existing projects are not silently migrated to rendering records or study levels. Source definitions stay immutable during a running session; preview controls are temporary copies.
Generated-output storage remains an ownership API; companion-map generation is not implemented. Calibration normal PNGs are original immutable fixtures kept outside the albedo palette.
Show-all-shape-outlines, per-shape lighting overrides and normal-map generator tools remain queued.

Color PNG validation and playback retain the existing opaque/1024px/16MiB/8M-pixel limits. The study separately decodes bounded raw normal data without tint/gamma/premultiplication; authoring currently validates companion paths rather than all data-map pixels.

Terrain normal-map rendering is enabled by an indexed static Lighting profile and compatible receiving builtin-lit material. Profiles without daylight use ambient only. Existing authored levels/assets are preserved; calendar profiles retain legacy unlit terrain until time projection is implemented.

World-light/calendar/weather projection, regional/indoor/event overrides, point/spot placement, cast shadows, gameplay-light queries, per-shape light overrides remain pending. Actor-controller and acoustic algorithms are unchanged; collision follows the corrected terrain raster.

Visual chunks cache albedo,8-bit world normals/roughness/specular/lighting weight and16-bit scalar emission over0–100. Seams mix an effective response. Light changes do not rebuild geometry; normal libraries are limited to8M unique pixels. This is a functional approximation, not a sustained performance claim.

Normal maps and scalar material parameters are bound; height, AO, roughness and emission map sampling and the companion-map generator remain pending. Image reload uses immutable session definitions; record changes require a fresh test.

Creator import preserves1107 PNG byte streams.803 opaque images within the1024px terrain limit are shared palette entries;300 non-opaque and4 oversized opaque images are retained in separate inspection folders and are not terrain fills.

Three compatibility IDs keep authored references and behavior hooks, but now use creator-provided stone/wood/moss images. Imported fills carry no invented physics/audio properties, normal maps or bevels. Categorization remains preliminary.

Metadata allows4096 rows per library. Active color images remain bounded to8M pixels; only current coverage is resident. Visible palette rows decode previews on demand with128 cached64px previews. Large simultaneous material sets can be refused without changing the draft.

Color-save validation is sequential with per-Workspace file-size/modification-time caching. This is not cryptographic integrity enforcement for subsequent external edits. Source PNG byte hashes were checked separately during import and packaging.

Unsafe engine-path filename characters were normalized; the public manifest retains original relative names and source hashes. Originals in the supplied source directory are untouched. General asset moves, automated re-import, shared-membership migration and alpha terrain rendering remain deferred.
Existing persistent projects are not silently migrated. Shared imported palettes are included in bundled content/new projects; controlled import into older projects remains a separate workflow.

Contour bevels are visual only. Optional shape overrides inherit indexed material defaults; width/depth use32px/m. Linear, round and concave profiles support Separate, Continuous or quarter-slope Soft seam contact modes against any occupied neighbor. Each side owns its response; texture blending and collision remain independent.

Bevels use bounded signed distances over2px authored coverage with bilinear sampling and gradient smoothing. The complete document must fit8M distance samples for a full rebuild even during incremental painting. Wide/many effects may be refused; no sustained performance claim.

Static level lighting supplies bevel illumination. Otherwise a registered lighting:bevel-default profile shades only visual relief while preserving the flat unlit interior. Projects without a supported profile or that fallback receive a refusal; no implicit migration or calendar evaluation.

Generated bevel normals are reoriented with authored detail normals. Enabled chunks add a separate8-bit geometry-normal/weight image; unbeveled terrain skips distance buffers and the extra image. Shadows, height-map relief, local lights and camera-independent illumination queries remain pending.

Material shape controls now include selected previews, searchable clipped thumbnail rows and hover-wheel selection. Closed editor dropdowns clamp at their endpoints; expanded lists scroll normally. Ctrl+wheel remains editor zoom. Source definition saves still require a fresh test session.

The native bevel course is a disposable demonstration with uniquely identified fixture materials and existing graphics. Existing levels, terrain files, assets and protected user sources are unchanged.

The sparse field now supports its full existing bounded world:4096 chunks across authored coordinates[-2048,2048)px. The old256-chunk prototype cap is removed. This is not unlimited terrain; source/history, texture and bevel work budgets still apply.

Square strokes use a continuous swept axis-aligned box. Round straight strokes remain capsules. Curves retain the selected square/round preset; replay of previously saved square curves intentionally uses the corrected square kernel. Geometry/collision contours still have2px raster resolution.

Terrain input observes captured UI releases without painting. A refused gesture reports a log error, clears its pending preview, restores published coverage and waits for release; redundant already-covered lines report no changed cells. No player-control or progression tuning was changed.

Celestial coordinates are east/up/north; normal-map lighting elevation has different semantics. The initial rendered moon is antipodal, without lunar phase/orbit. Raw equal-month seasonal phase is smooth while existing Weather selection remains whole-second and unchanged.

Atmosphere is effective level weather before indoor suppression and retains level/external modifiers. Simulation time drives cloud animation and future card/wave effects; calendar time drives celestial phase. Failed snapshots return unavailable/diagnostic output without cancelling gameplay modal state.

Sky is opt-in through a registered sky_profile and explicit level attachment. Existing source levels/assets remain unchanged. The new course uses a transparent background; opaque authored backgrounds legitimately conceal the reserved-first sky pass.

Horizon altitude_parallax defaults to0.01 (1%):1m horizon movement per100m foreground movement. Values are editable through Skies. Level attachment supplies explicit native Y origin and pixel/metre scale; no hidden origin migration.

Clouds use one fixed four-octave procedural layer with authored night brightness and weather mappings. Motion integrates simulation deltas without restarting on wind changes. Sky shader failure has a nonfatal gradient fallback. No sustained performance certification is claimed.

Cycle settings are now explicit sky profile data. The initial moon remains antipodal without lunar phase/orbit. Stars, background composition/layer templates and tools, foliage cards, water/reactions and sky-driven terrain lighting remain later work.

Palette colors interpolate in authored sRGB. Definition edits apply to a fresh test rather than silently changing the immutable running snapshot. No external editor/browser toolchain or Python testing framework is shipped.

reference.use: Original database/item/message/choice/switch/variable organization and common-event Name/Execution/Switch/Event Commands groups; native controls bind existing authoritative services. Fields adapt the original Weather Effects Type/Power grouping while retaining the native wind model.
